title: Naḥw and ṣarf at al-Azhar and in the Maghrib
summary: From al-Ājurrūmiyya to the Alfiyya: the Arab and North-African path climbs through Ibn Hishām's graded books.

sections.heading: The naḥw ladder
paragraphs: The student memorises al-Ājurrūmiyya and reads it with a commentary, then Qaṭr al-nadā and Shudhūr al-dhahab of Ibn Hishām. The summit is Ibn Mālik's Alfiyya, read with Ibn ʿAqīl's commentary or Ibn Hishām's Awḍaḥ al-masālik, and for the advanced Mughnī al-labīb.
In the Maghrib and Mauritania the Alfiyya is memorised in full, and al-Ājurrūmiyya is often learnt in a versified form.

sections.heading: Ṣarf
paragraphs: Ṣarf is read in al-Taṣrīf al-ʿIzzī and Ibn Mālik's Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl, and in modern al-Azhar in al-Ḥamalāwī's Shadhā al-ʿarf. Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Shāfiya with the commentary of Raḍī al-Dīn stands at the top.
The Nahwi's North-African path follows this ladder.
